messages.content: What's the lowest score in the Flappy Bird game?

function.name: game_tracker_high_score

game_name.description: The name of the game to get the high score for.

username.description: The username of the player. (optional) Default: 'john'

message.content:
In *Flappy Bird* the very first thing that happens is that your bird starts flying from the left side of the screen. You earn a point **only** once you successfully fly past a set of pipes.  
If you crash into a wall, ground, or an invisible boundary before getting through even the first pair of pipes, you never receive that first point – your total stays at **zero**.

So:

| Situation | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Immediate collision (before passing any pipes) | **0** |
| Passes at least one pair of pipes | ≥ 1 |

There isn’t really a “record” for the lowest score other than this trivial outcome—any play session that ends without clearing a single pipe will always end at 0 points.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What's the lowest score in the Flappy Bird game?" They want presumably the minimum possible score or maybe they mean what is the lowest score achieved historically? But likely it's asking about the lowest score you can achieve - which would be zero if you die immediately after starting.

But we have a tool `game_tracker_high_score` but that's only for retrieving high scores; not low scores. There's no direct tool for lowest score. We could interpret as "lowest score" meaning minimal score someone got before dying. That might be 0. So answer: 0 points. Or explain that the lowest possible score is 0 because you lose instantly when hitting something.

We should respond with explanation and mention that there's no official record for lowest score beyond trivial case. Also note that Flappy Bird's scoring increments per pipe passed so first pass gives at least one point. Actually initial start yields 1 point on passing first pair. If you hit obstacle right away, you may still get 0? In many versions, you don't get a point until you pass a pair. So immediate death results in 0. So lowest score is 0.

Thus reply accordingly. No need to call function.
